decision: per-line content hashes + a window scan, no AST.
why: Add tree-sitter when a real repo produces orphans this cannot explain.

A 3k-line file against a 10-line span is ~30k hash comparisons — microseconds, and it only runs on records that already failed both cheap checks. Revisit if capture ever starts anchoring records to spans hundreds of lines long.

decision: 4 hex chars, matching the #4f2a shape the README uses.
why: ~65k values, so a collision becomes likely around a few hundred records; nothing keys off the id yet, so a duplicate is cosmetic today. Widen when `why check` starts citing ids in CI output.

decision: comment syntax by prefix, not by parser.
why: Covers //, # and block- comment continuations, which is every language in this repo. A note inside a language that comments some other way is simply not harvested — silent, but silent-and-absent rather than silent-and-wrong.

Real relevance ranking (does this record concern the lines actually being changed? has it been contradicted before?) needs the diff, which PreToolUse does not have. Revisit when `why check` exists in Phase 2.

decision: this counts SURFACINGS, not caught contradictions, so it over-counts — most surfacings are purely informational.
why: The DECISIONS §8 falsification number needs `why check` comparing a diff against records (Phase 2). Do not read this file as the falsification metric.

decision: whole-file JSON read and a linear scan in Match.
why: Fine at the ~20 hand-written records of Phase 0 (microseconds). Move to SQLite with an index on (file, line_start, line_end) once Phase 1 capture makes this thousands of records, because PreToolUse blocks every edit and latency becomes visible.
